## Findings ledger
- [D3.DOC31.F5] Bendix reads Weber’s scholarship as combining political and moral commitment with analytic detachment, rather than as value-free indifference — dim: theme_position — anchor: "This combination of commitment and detachment was yet another aspect of the personal and intellectual tensions that marred his life and made it creative." — doc: em:PL4C6Y9V — reader: Reinhard Bendix — theme-origin: plan_spine — theme: Science, political values and responsibility — plan-theme-link: Science, political values and responsibility — position: Weber’s scientific work is presented as simultaneously committed to reason and freedom and disciplined by detachment from immediate political identification — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes
- [D3.DOC31.F6] Bendix adds empirical reconstruction as a methodological concern, arguing that Weber’s substantive investigations should take priority over isolated methodological definitions when interpreting his sociology — dim: theme_position — anchor: "the present study approaches Weber’s work with a major emphasis on his empirical rather than his methodological writings." — doc: em:PL4C6Y9V — reader: Reinhard Bendix — theme-origin: reader_addition — theme: Empirical reconstruction over methodological abstraction — plan-theme-link: outside-spine — position: Bendix’s reading privileges Weber’s empirical studies as the primary route to understanding his concepts and comparative arguments — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

scope_outcomes.criterion: A secondary reader must make an anchored interpretive claim about Max Weber on a supplied engagement theme or a clearly labelled reader-added theme.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected excerpt contains anchored interpretations by Reinhard Bendix concerning class and status-group concepts, domination and political organization, bureaucracy and patrimonial rule, subjective meaning, science, values, commitment, detachment, and empirical reconstruction.
limitations: The source is a bounded excerpt rather than the complete book.
The excerpt does not directly address political capitalism, imperialism, or tax-farming.
No claim is made about Bendix’s complete treatment of the remaining themes outside the inspected sections.
